correctness.rationale: PASS. In the Cartesian product of cliques every geodesic changes each coordinate at most once. Its active binary endpoint words form a monotone prefix chain; the distance of binary word a to the path equals number of ones minus the maximum of prefix walk sums. A reflection-principle count by maximum m and number of ones gives B_L(z)=sum_j (L-2j+1)[C(L,j)-C(L,j-1)]z^j including L=0. Every unchanged coordinate contributes 1+(q_i-1)z and every active coordinate taking a third symbol contributes the constant distance 1, giving the complete product/subset polynomial. Degree and explicit farthest vertices yield ecc=d-ceil(s/2) for s active binary coordinates; minimization over s and reversal-paired path counting prove the stated optimizer sets and exact numbers, separately counting singleton geodesics at b=0. A new independent direct vertex-geodesic distance enumerator matched 216 mixed binary/nonbinary cases, including order invariance. These checks corroborate rather than replace the all-product proof.
residual_risks: The geodesic is allowed to be a singleton; reversal count needs separate handling there.
Applies only to Cartesian products of complete graphs.
